reference_answer: You've got some skill; if you dare, come meet me at the mountaintop.

db_evidence.notes: The exact reference quote '有种跟我来山顶会合！' is present verbatim as plain text in episodes:30sec:000222 (start_s=6660, end_s=6690) and episodes:3min:000037, retrievable by a simple SQL scan of the episodes table around the clue window -- no clip_qa was strictly necessary. However, that row's caption labels the defeated boss '妖王·黄眉大王' (a different boss name) rather than '黑风大王', while the entities table's black-wind-king row (entities:000046) is bounded start_s=6450..end_s=6660, i.e. its window ends exactly where the correct answer row begins. This name mismatch plus the entity boundary sitting right at 6660 appears to have caused 3/5 rollouts to distrust or route around the correct text evidence and either re-scope clip_qa to a window that (barely) excluded the clue interval, or chase an entirely different, later 'boss defeated' scene (~7500s, a different character) that is lore-adjacent (also a Journey-to-the-West black-bear-type villain) and superficially similar in the DB.

root_causes: Caption/entity inconsistency: the correct scene's episodes-table caption names the boss '黄眉大王' instead of '黑风大王', and the entities-table boundary for '黑风大王' ends at exactly 6660s (the start of the correct row) -- both push the agent away from evidence that is otherwise textually correct and sufficient by itself.

Over-reliance on clip_qa despite already holding correct SQL text evidence: 3/5 rollouts saw the exact reference quote in a run_sql result and still deferred to a subsequent clip_qa call, then let a mis-scoped clip_qa transcription overwrite the correct text.

Clip window mis-scoping right at the clue boundary: rollout-1's window (6600-6660) and rollout-3's window (6580-6665) both stop just before/at the clue interval start (6666), landing on adjacent but wrong dialogue (combat taunts / unrelated lines) instead of the post-defeat line.

Reused-boss-template confusion: a later, unrelated 'boss defeated' scene around 7500s in the DB (different character, thematically similar Journey-to-the-West black-bear villain) was semantically close enough to mislead rollout-0's semantic/SQL search entirely off the correct time window.

Visual sub-agent under-sampling: rollout-4's clip_qa found the right window and the right first clause of the line but stopped sampling frames before the second clause appeared, producing a partial (5->3 scored) answer.
what_worked: Rollout-2 issued a clip_qa window (6630-6690) that fully bracketed the clue interval and explicitly asked the sub-agent to distinguish the boss name from any other boss name shown, and its evidence_times_s (6662-6670) landed inside the clue interval, yielding the essentially verbatim reference answer.
transferable_lessons: When a run_sql/semantic_search result already contains an apparent verbatim quote matching the question, prefer that text evidence over a subsequent clip_qa call scoped to a different or narrower window; don't let a later visual-agent transcription silently override already-correct textual evidence without reconciling the discrepancy.

When scoping a clip_qa window around a 'what does X say right after Y' question, pad generously past the located anchor time (e.g. a defeat marker) rather than stopping exactly at or just before it -- off-by-a-few-seconds windows reliably miss the target line here.

Treat boss/character name mismatches between adjacent DB rows (e.g. a caption naming a different boss right after the entity's stated end boundary) as a caption/labeling artifact to double-check via a wider SQL time scan, not as proof of a different, unrelated scene.

When a scene has multiple similarly-themed encounters (e.g. reused boss templates or lore-similar characters) elsewhere in the timeline, anchor tightly to the question's specific named entity's own bounded interval rather than semantic-searching broadly and picking up a distant, similarly-worded scene.

For multi-clause spoken lines, instruct clip_qa to keep sampling forward past the first detected subtitle until a scene cut or clear line-end, since a single clip_qa call can truncate mid-quote and yield a partially-correct answer.
open_questions: Whether the '黄眉大王' vs '黑风大王' name discrepancy in the episodes caption for row 000222 is a captioning/OCR error in the memory-database build pipeline, or reflects an actual in-game boss-name change/alias at that moment -- this determines whether the fix belongs in the retrieval agent's skepticism or in the database captioning.
